ai_summary: Great Britain's electricity system is currently operating with 11.7 GW of total wind generation, of which Scottish wind contributes an estimated 1.0 GW, representing 9.9% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Generation mix differences are stark across regions, with Scottish carbon intensity standing at 0 gCO2/kWh compared to 59 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. Despite Scotland producing entirely clean power, transmission boundaries continue to enforce localized bottlenecks. So far today, 204 MWh of Scottish generation has been turned down through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £6,641. To replace this curtailed low-carbon volume, thermal generation elsewhere in the network burned an estimated 38,741 m3 of natural gas, resulting in an additional 71 tonnes of carbon emissions. Extrapolating today’s curtailment rate gives an estimated total yearly constraint cost of approximately £2 million to the nearest million. When spread across aggregate national electricity demand, this adds an estimated increase of less than £0.01/MWh to UK electricity invoices, demonstrating that while the broader consumer bill impact from today's specific actions remains small, the cumulative emissions and system balancing inefficiencies persist.
